decks.domain: Preparing to drive and driver factors

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Before driving, check that the tires have sufficient?
cards.back: Before driving, check that the tires have sufficient tread and the correct air pressure.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use the tire-pressure value in the owner's manual or driver-side door?
cards.back: Use the tire-pressure value in the owner's manual or driver-side door jamb and check it with a pressure gauge.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Check tire pressure when the tires are cold, before driving?
cards.back: Check tire pressure when the tires are cold, before driving or at least three hours after driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If measured pressure is above the specified value, release air until it?
cards.back: If measured pressure is above the specified value, release air until it matches; if below, add air or seek tire-professional help.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Inspect tires for wear and damage once a month?
cards.back: Inspect tires for wear and damage once a month or before a long road trip.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: For the penny tread check, hold Lincoln's body and insert his?
cards.back: For the penny tread check, hold Lincoln's body and insert his head into a groove where the tread appears lowest.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: In the handbook's penny test, tread covering any part of Lincoln's?
cards.back: In the handbook's penny test, tread covering any part of Lincoln's head indicates the stated safe amount of tread.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Tread below the penny-test level greatly reduces?
cards.back: Tread below the penny-test level greatly reduces tire grip in adverse conditions.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Keep tire-changing equipment in the vehicle, including a spare, lug wrench, jack,?
cards.back: Keep tire-changing equipment in the vehicle, including a spare, lug wrench, jack, flashlight, warning devices, wheel wedges, repair kit and gloves.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Check oil, washer fluid and fuel, and refill?
cards.back: Check oil, washer fluid and fuel, and refill as the owner's manual directs.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Set the driver's seat so the pedals and controls are easy?
cards.back: Set the driver's seat so the pedals and controls are easy to reach and the windshield view is clear.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Wear both the lap belt and shoulder?
cards.back: Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt on every trip.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Loose objects can become projectiles in a crash while?
cards.back: Loose objects can become projectiles in a crash while continuing at the vehicle's pre-impact speed.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Put heavy objects in the trunk when possible,?
cards.back: Put heavy objects in the trunk when possible, or secure them with seat belts.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not place stored objects on?
cards.back: Do not place stored objects on the rear window deck.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Adjust the seat before?
cards.back: Adjust the seat before setting the mirrors.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Set the rearview mirror to show traffic?
cards.back: Set the rearview mirror to show traffic directly behind the vehicle.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Set side mirrors so the vehicle's side is barely?
cards.back: Set side mirrors so the vehicle's side is barely visible when leaning toward that side.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Mirror settings may need to differ between?
cards.back: Mirror settings may need to differ between drivers to remove blind spots.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not hang objects from the rearview mirror?
cards.back: Do not hang objects from the rearview mirror while the vehicle is moving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Tags, permits and placards may hang from the rearview?
cards.back: Tags, permits and placards may hang from the rearview mirror only while the vehicle is parked.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Nothing may be attached to the windshield where?
cards.back: Nothing may be attached to the windshield where it obstructs the driver's road view.

decks.domain: Preparing to drive and driver factors

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Maintain fresh air in the vehicle to support alertness?
cards.back: Maintain fresh air in the vehicle to support alertness and guard against exhaust-related carbon monoxide poisoning.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Set the head restraint so its top reaches at least the?
cards.back: Set the head restraint so its top reaches at least the height of the top of the driver's ears.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A properly positioned head restraint can prevent or?
cards.back: A properly positioned head restraint can prevent or reduce neck-injury severity in a crash.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Always use prescription glasses or contacts while driving?
cards.back: Always use prescription glasses or contacts while driving if you normally wear corrective lenses.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not use sunglasses or tinted contact?
cards.back: Do not use sunglasses or tinted contact lenses for night driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Locking the doors and wearing a seat belt help?
cards.back: Locking the doors and wearing a seat belt help prevent being thrown out during a crash.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Locked doors also reduce the likelihood of victimization when?
cards.back: Locked doors also reduce the likelihood of victimization when stopped at an intersection or parking area.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A driving distraction takes attention from driving, eyes from?
cards.back: A driving distraction takes attention from driving, eyes from the road or hands from the wheel.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Eating, drinking or smoking can draw hands and eyes away?
cards.back: Eating, drinking or smoking can draw hands and eyes away from driving and slow the response to hazards.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Adjusting audio equipment is?
cards.back: Adjusting audio equipment is a driving distraction.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Headphones or earpieces may be used in only?
cards.back: Headphones or earpieces may be used in only one ear and only for communication.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A phone conversation can distract a driver even?
cards.back: A phone conversation can distract a driver even when the phone is hands-free.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Interacting with passengers can?
cards.back: Interacting with passengers can distract the driver.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Searching for or moving an item inside?
cards.back: Searching for or moving an item inside the vehicle is a distraction.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Reading, writing, texting and personal grooming can?
cards.back: Reading, writing, texting and personal grooming can divert attention from driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Staring at a crash, work zone or an?
cards.back: Staring at a crash, work zone or an off-road event can distract a driver.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Tiredness slows reactions and impairs?
cards.back: Tiredness slows reactions and impairs judgment and vision.

decks.domain: Preparing to drive and driver factors

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Fatigued driving can affect a driver in?
cards.back: Fatigued driving can affect a driver in ways similar to alcohol impairment.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The handbook compares eighteen hours awake with about the driving impairment associated?
cards.back: The handbook compares eighteen hours awake with about the driving impairment associated with a point zero five percent blood alcohol level.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The handbook compares twenty-four continuous hours awake with impairment associated with?
cards.back: The handbook compares twenty-four continuous hours awake with impairment associated with a point one zero percent blood alcohol level.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A sufficiently tired driver may fall?
cards.back: A sufficiently tired driver may fall asleep without realizing it.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Even a few seconds asleep at the?
cards.back: Even a few seconds asleep at the wheel can be fatal.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Teenagers sleeping less than eight hours nightly?
cards.back: Teenagers sleeping less than eight hours nightly face increased vehicle-crash risk.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If tiredness develops while driving, the?
cards.back: If tiredness develops while driving, the handbook recommends stopping driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Vision should be checked every?
cards.back: Vision should be checked every one or two years.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Disease and aging can worsen side vision, distance judgment?
cards.back: Disease and aging can worsen side vision, distance judgment and low-light vision without the driver noticing.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use required glasses or contact lenses every?
cards.back: Use required glasses or contact lenses every time the vehicle is driven.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Hearing can reveal unseen hazards, approaching emergency?
cards.back: Hearing can reveal unseen hazards, approaching emergency vehicles and trains at crossings.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Medical problems, including a stiff neck or sore knee,?
cards.back: Medical problems, including a stiff neck or sore knee, can interfere with effective vehicle control.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Seizure disorders involving loss of consciousness, diabetes and heart conditions are among?
cards.back: Seizure disorders involving loss of consciousness, diabetes and heart conditions are among the serious driving-related health problems identified by the handbook.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Pennsylvania physicians must report to PennDOT people they diagnose with?
cards.back: Pennsylvania physicians must report to PennDOT people they diagnose with a condition that could impair safe driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Drivers younger than twenty-one are considered to be driving under the influence at a?
cards.back: Drivers younger than twenty-one are considered to be driving under the influence at a blood alcohol concentration of point zero two percent or higher.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Even a small amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception,?
cards.back: Even a small amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment and memory and impair driving skills.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: As blood alcohol rises, driving errors increase while vision,?
cards.back: As blood alcohol rises, driving errors increase while vision, judgment, reactions and vehicle control deteriorate.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Alcohol can produce dangerous confidence while reducing?
cards.back: Alcohol can produce dangerous confidence while reducing the driver's actual skills.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The handbook describes point zero eight percent as the legal blood?
cards.back: The handbook describes point zero eight percent as the legal blood alcohol limit for an adult aged twenty-one or older.

decks.domain: Preparing to drive and driver factors

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Alcohol in the blood can make driving dangerous?
cards.back: Alcohol in the blood can make driving dangerous even below the legal limit.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The handbook states that the safe amount of?
cards.back: The handbook states that the safe amount of alcohol before driving is zero.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Age, weight, gender, physical condition, food and drugs?
cards.back: Age, weight, gender, physical condition, food and drugs or medication affect blood alcohol levels.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Drinks can contain different amounts of alcohol,?
cards.back: Drinks can contain different amounts of alcohol, so their alcohol content matters.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The handbook's standard-drink examples are one point five ounces of eighty-proof liquor, twelve?
cards.back: The handbook's standard-drink examples are one point five ounces of eighty-proof liquor, twelve ounces of regular beer or five ounces of wine.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: For a person of average weight, the handbook says processing the?
cards.back: For a person of average weight, the handbook says processing the alcohol in one drink takes at least one hour.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The handbook advises legal-age drinkers not to exceed one drink per hour, while warning that this guideline?
cards.back: The handbook advises legal-age drinkers not to exceed one drink per hour, while warning that this guideline does not work for everyone and does not make driving after drinking safe.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Alcohol is more concentrated?
cards.back: Alcohol is more concentrated in smaller people.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A woman may reach a higher blood alcohol level than a same-weight?
cards.back: A woman may reach a higher blood alcohol level than a same-weight man after equal alcohol intake over the same time.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Only time lowers blood alcohol concentration; coffee, other caffeine drinks?
cards.back: Only time lowers blood alcohol concentration; coffee, other caffeine drinks and cold showers do not reduce it.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not drive after consuming any alcohol, and prevent a?
cards.back: Do not drive after consuming any alcohol, and prevent a person who has been drinking from driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Illegal drugs, prescription medicines and over-the-counter products?
cards.back: Illegal drugs, prescription medicines and over-the-counter products can all impair driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Combining drugs with alcohol intensifies side effects?
cards.back: Combining drugs with alcohol intensifies side effects and greatly increases crash risk.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Marijuana can slow reactions, impair time and?
cards.back: Marijuana can slow reactions, impair time and distance judgment and reduce coordination.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Cocaine or methamphetamine can make a?
cards.back: Cocaine or methamphetamine can make a driver aggressive and reckless.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Certain sedatives can cause?
cards.back: Certain sedatives can cause dizziness and drowsiness.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Opioids can cause drowsiness?
cards.back: Opioids can cause drowsiness and slower reactions.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Sleeping pills, cough medicines, antihistamines and decongestants?
cards.back: Sleeping pills, cough medicines, antihistamines and decongestants can affect driving skills.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Read medicine warning labels for?
cards.back: Read medicine warning labels for side effects before driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Ask a doctor or pharmacist about uncertain?
cards.back: Ask a doctor or pharmacist about uncertain medication side effects before driving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A warning against operating heavy machinery applies?
cards.back: A warning against operating heavy machinery applies to driving a vehicle.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When starting a new medication, consult the doctor?
cards.back: When starting a new medication, consult the doctor and learn its potential side effects.
